title: Broken pieces in the set
hook: Would you price the same dinnerware sets differently alone and side by side?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish separate evaluation from joint comparison of total usable pieces.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish separate evaluation from joint comparison of total usable pieces.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy dinner set contains forty pieces, nine broken. How many usable pieces are available? Toy inputs A=[40, 9]; B=[24, 0].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[31, 77.5, 40], [24, 100, 24]]. Labels: Usable pieces, Usable %, Total pieces.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The larger set can have more usable pieces while a smaller fraction of its pieces is intact. Joint comparison makes those two dimensions explicit. A separate valuation may focus on either dimension, so a quality fraction is not a count.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Total pieces=24, Broken pieces=0. What is Usable pieces? Answer: 24.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Total pieces=24, Broken pieces=0. What is Usable pieces?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 24. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Viewed alone, a 24-piece dinnerware set was valued at $33 versus $23 for a 40-piece set with some broken pieces; side by side, the larger set won (Hsee, 1998).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish separate evaluation from joint comparison of total usable pieces.
